journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
title: A Single-Cell Atlas of the Human Healthy Airways.
claim_supported: scRNA-seq of 77,969 cells from nose to 12th airway division in 10 healthy volunteers, including nasal brushings: 89% epithelial, 6% immune and 5% stromal cells.

title: Single-Cell Analysis Reveals the Range of Transcriptional States of Circulating Human Neutrophils.
claim_supported: Claim 12 (partial): scRNA-seq of human neutrophils is technically difficult, and changing the data-analysis pipeline (not the chemistry) greatly increases neutrophil detection; the abstract does not give gene counts.

title: Prolonged activation of nasal immune cell populations and development of tissue-resident SARS-CoV-2-specific CD8+ T cell responses following COVID-19.
claim_supported: Claim 12 (partial): nasal granulocytes/neutrophils are present in human nasal mucosal samples and rise during acute COVID-19 (flow cytometry, not scRNA-seq).

title: UCell: Robust and scalable single-cell gene signature scoring.
claim_supported: Claim 13: UCell scores gene signatures in single cells with the Mann-Whitney U statistic and is robust to dataset size and heterogeneity.

title: Orchestrating single-cell analysis with Bioconductor.
claim_supported: Claim 8: overview of the Bioconductor single-cell workflow and the OSCA online book (the usual citation for adaptive MAD-based outlier QC); the abstract itself does not mention MAD thresholds.

title: UCell and pyUCell: single-cell gene signature scoring for R and Python.
claim_supported: Claim 13: UCell (R) and pyUCell (Python) implement rank-based single-cell signature scoring compatible with scanpy/scverse.

title: Systematic determination of the mitochondrial proportion in human and mice tissues for single-cell RNA-sequencing data quality control.
claim_supported: Claim 8: across 5.5 million cells mtDNA% is higher in human than mouse tissues and a uniform 5% threshold fails in 13 of 44 human tissues, so tissue-specific mitochondrial thresholds are needed.

title: Defective epithelial barrier in chronic rhinosinusitis: the regulation of tight junctions by IFN-γ and IL-4.
claim_supported: In human sinonasal epithelium, CRS with nasal polyps shows lower trans-tissue resistance and lower occludin and ZO-1 (TJP1), and IFN-gamma and IL-4 reduce barrier integrity in primary nasal ALI cultures.

title: Tight junctions: from simple barriers to multifunctional molecular gates.
claim_supported: Tight junctions form selective paracellular barriers in epithelia, mark the apical/basolateral border and connect to signalling networks and other adhesion complexes.

journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
title: The effect of aging on nasal mucociliary clearance, beat frequency, and ultrastructure of respiratory cilia.
claim_supported: In healthy volunteers aged 11-90, nasal ciliary beat frequency fell and mucociliary clearance time and microtubular abnormalities rose with age (functional and ultrastructural data, not transcriptomic).

title: Novel dynamics of human mucociliary differentiation revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing of nasal epithelial cultures.
claim_supported: scRNA-seq of human nasal epithelial cultures traces basal-to-multiciliated differentiation via deuterosomal cells and finds hybrid goblet/multiciliated cells (so ciliary genes can appear in secretory-like cells).

title: Impaired local intrinsic immunity to SARS-CoV-2 infection in severe COVID-19.
claim_supported: During COVID-19 nasopharyngeal samples show loss of ciliated and expansion of secretory cells, so ciliary module scores at sample level partly reflect cell composition and infection.

title: Foxj1 transcription factors are master regulators of the motile ciliogenic program.
claim_supported: Foxj1 activates genes essential for motile cilia formation and is sufficient for ectopic motile-like cilia (zebrafish).

title: Motile ciliopathies.
claim_supported: Mutations that impair motile-cilia beating cause motile ciliopathies including primary ciliary dyskinesia with impaired respiratory mucociliary clearance (the individual gene list is not in the abstract).

title: CFTR expression decreases with age in several airway cell types.
claim_supported: In public bulk and single-cell lung data CFTR expression in goblet, club and basal cells fell with age (not ciliated cells); evidence that airway secretory-cell programmes change with age (not mucin genes themselves).

title: Novel dynamics of human mucociliary differentiation revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing of nasal epithelial cultures.
claim_supported: Claim 7: upper airway epithelium contains distinct multiciliated, goblet, club and basal cells; goblet cells can be precursors of multiciliated cells, explaining hybrid goblet/ciliated cells.

title: Allergic inflammatory memory in human respiratory epithelial progenitor cells.
claim_supported: scRNA-seq of human sinonasal tissue and nasal scrapings defined core, healthy, inflamed and polyp secretory-cell signatures, with secretory antimicrobial programmes shifting in type 2 inflammation.

title: A molecular cell atlas of the human lung from single-cell RNA sequencing.
claim_supported: Claim 7 (partial): human lung and airway scRNA-seq atlas defining the expression profiles of 58 cell populations; the abstract does not itself state goblet-versus-club differences.

journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
title: A Single-Cell Atlas of the Human Healthy Airways.
claim_supported: Claim 7 (related): the same cell types (suprabasal, secretory, multiciliated) differ between nose (MUC4, PI3, SIX3) and tracheobronchial airways (SCGB1A1, TFF3), so SCGB1A1 is a weaker secretory marker in nasal brushings.

title: Muc5b is required for airway defence.
claim_supported: MUC5AC and MUC5B encode the principal airway mucins; Muc5b (not Muc5ac) is required for mucociliary clearance and airway defence in mice, and MUC5B at human airway surfaces can fall by up to 90% in disease.

title: Airway mucus function and dysfunction.
claim_supported: Review of airway mucus and mucin function and dysfunction in airway disease (no abstract in PubMed; content not checked).

title: Early rise in nasal secretory IgA associated with shorter duration of SARS-CoV-2 virus shedding in an acute infection cohort.
claim_supported: In 143 people with acute SARS-CoV-2, an early rise in nasal-lavage secretory IgA (especially anti-spike NTD) was associated with shorter viral shedding (association only).

journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
title: Bronchial secretory immunoglobulin a deficiency correlates with airway inflammation and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
claim_supported: In human bronchi normal ciliated epithelium expresses pIgR with surface SIgA, remodelled epithelium has reduced pIgR and local SIgA deficiency, and full epithelial differentiation is needed for pIgR expression and IgA transcytosis.

title: Mucosal immunity: induction, dissemination, and effector functions.
claim_supported: Claim 9: secretory IgA is mainly dimeric IgA made by local plasma cells and transported by pIgR, the only receptor for epithelial IgA/IgM transport in pIgR-deficient mice; airways receive B cells primed in nasopharynx-associated lymphoid tissue.

title: The polymeric immunoglobulin receptor: bridging innate and adaptive immune responses at mucosal surfaces.
claim_supported: pIgR mediates epithelial transcytosis of polymeric IgA; its cleaved secretory component is released free or as part of SIgA; pIgR expression is regulated by TLR signalling and cytokines.

title: Role of J chain in secretory immunoglobulin formation.
claim_supported: Claim 9: only J-chain-containing IgA/IgM polymers bind pIgR with high affinity, and SIgA and free secretory component come from cleavage of the pIgR extracellular domain.

title: Regulation of the polymeric immunoglobulin receptor and IgA transport: new advances in environmental factors that stimulate pIgR expression and its role in mucosal immunity.
claim_supported: pIgR transports locally produced dimeric IgA across mucosal epithelia and is the precursor of secretory component, with expression regulated by host and microbial factors.

title: Receptor-mediated immunoglobulin G transport across mucosal barriers in adult life: functional expression of FcRn in the mammalian lung.
claim_supported: Adult human, non-human primate and mouse bronchial epithelial cells express FcRn, and FcRn transports IgG-Fc across mouse respiratory epithelium in vivo.

title: FcRn: the neonatal Fc receptor comes of age.
claim_supported: FcRn transports IgG (maternal-fetal transfer), protects IgG from degradation and is expressed at various sites in adults.

title: Pre-activated antiviral innate immunity in the upper airways controls early SARS-CoV-2 infection in children.
claim_supported: Claims 1 and 3: upper-airway scRNA-seq (4 weeks to 77 years) showed higher basal expression of the PRRs MDA5 (IFIH1) and RIG-I (DDX58) in children's epithelial cells, macrophages and DCs than in adults.

title: Age-dependent dysregulation of innate immunity.
claim_supported: With age innate immunity becomes dysregulated: basal inflammation rises (partly from endogenous DAMPs acting on PRRs) while PRR signalling and cell migration needed for pathogen and vaccine responses are impaired.

journal: Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol
title: Innate immunity in the respiratory epithelium.
claim_supported: Airway epithelium expresses many innate immune receptors including TLRs and NOD-like receptors, which drive cytokine/chemokine production and recruit neutrophils and T cells.

title: IFN-alpha enhances TLR3-mediated antiviral cytokine expression in human endothelial and epithelial cells by up-regulating TLR3 expression.
claim_supported: TLR7 and TLR8 were not expressed in human A549 epithelial cells, so endosomal TLR7 in M04 will mostly reflect immune cells rather than epithelium (cell-line data).

title: A diverse range of gene products are effectors of the type I interferon antiviral response.
claim_supported: C6orf150/MB21D1 (CGAS) was in the ISG library and was a broadly acting antiviral ISG, so CGAS is interferon-inducible and not purely a constitutive sensor.

title: Pattern recognition receptors and inflammation.
claim_supported: Innate sensing is mediated by PRR families (TLRs, RIG-I-like receptors, NOD-like receptors, C-type lectins) that signal to inflammatory gene expression.

title: Shared and unique functions of the DExD/H-box helicases RIG-I, MDA5, and LGP2 in antiviral innate immunity.
claim_supported: RIG-I and MDA5 sense viral RNA and signal via their CARDs to induce type I IFN, whereas LGP2 lacks CARDs and acts as a negative regulator (relevant to the excluded RLR genes).

title: cGAS in action: Expanding roles in immunity and inflammation.
claim_supported: The cGAS-STING pathway detects intracellular DNA from pathogens and from self (DAMP) and mediates inflammatory responses, including sterile inflammation.

title: Pre-activated antiviral innate immunity in the upper airways controls early SARS-CoV-2 infection in children.
claim_supported: Claim 3: children's upper airway cells are primed for virus sensing, with higher basal IFIH1/DDX58 and stronger early innate antiviral responses than adults.

title: Aging-related cell type-specific pathophysiologic immune responses that exacerbate disease severity in aged COVID-19 patients.
claim_supported: Older people with severe COVID-19 showed type I and II IFN deficiencies and reduced antiviral defence genes (LY6E, IFNAR1) in nasal secretory cells (integrative re-analysis of public data).

title: Local and systemic responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection in children and adults.
claim_supported: Claim 3: single-cell profiling of nasal, tracheal and bronchial samples showed that airway cells of healthy children are already in an interferon-activated state compared with adults.

title: Interferon-λ Mediates Non-redundant Front-Line Antiviral Protection against Influenza Virus Infection without Compromising Host Fitness.
claim_supported: Claim 2: in mouse influenza infection IFN-lambdas are the first IFNs produced and act at the respiratory epithelial barrier to suppress initial spread without inflammation, with type I IFN acting later (mouse data).

title: Role of double-stranded RNA pattern recognition receptors in rhinovirus-induced airway epithelial cell responses.
claim_supported: Claim 1 (airway context): rhinovirus infection of human bronchial epithelial cells induced IFN-beta, IFN-lambda1/2/3, IRF7, RIG-I and MDA5 mRNA in a TLR3/TRIF-, MDA5- and IRF3-dependent way.

title: Lambda interferon is the predominant interferon induced by influenza A virus infection in vivo.
claim_supported: Claim 2: after intranasal influenza A infection in mice type III IFN levels greatly exceed type I in the lung, and the IFN-lambda receptor is expressed mainly by epithelial cells (mouse data).

title: Impaired local intrinsic immunity to SARS-CoV-2 infection in severe COVID-19.
claim_supported: scRNA-seq of nasopharyngeal swabs from 58 people: mild/moderate COVID-19 epithelial cells express antiviral/IFN-responsive genes while severe cases have muted responses; infection also changes epithelial composition (secretory up, ciliated down).

title: Dynamic innate immune response determines susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection and early replication kinetics.
claim_supported: In serial human nasopharyngeal samples SARS-CoV-2 induced ISGs in the upper respiratory tract, and prior rhinovirus infection accelerated ISG responses and blocked SARS-CoV-2 replication, so baseline nasal ISG state depends on recent infections.

title: Type I interferons in infectious disease.
claim_supported: Type I IFNs are protective against viruses but can cause immunopathology in acute infections and immunosuppression in chronic infections, so a high ISG score is not simply 'better immunity'.

title: A diverse range of gene products are effectors of the type I interferon antiviral response.
claim_supported: Full text: the compiled library of 389 ISGs included PSMB8, PSMB9, MX1, IFIT3, IFI6, IFITM3, BST2, IRF7, RSAD2 and also CDKN1A (toxic on overexpression), so CDKN1A is IFN-inducible and overlaps the ISG and senescence modules.

title: Interferon-stimulated genes: a complex web of host defenses.
claim_supported: ISG products enhance pathogen sensing, negatively regulate JAK-STAT signalling and directly inhibit viruses (review of ISG biology).

title: Differential roles for the interferon-inducible IFI16 and AIM2 innate immune sensors for cytosolic DNA in cellular senescence of human fibroblasts.
claim_supported: Claim 1: AIM2 is an IFN-inducible cytosolic DNA sensor; IFN-beta treatment induced AIM2 protein in human fibroblasts, and AIM2 rose in senescent fibroblasts with IL-1beta.

title: RNA- and virus-independent inhibition of antiviral signaling by RNA helicase LGP2.
claim_supported: Claim 1: LGP2 (DHX58) mRNA is induced by interferon, dsRNA or Sendai virus and acts as a feedback inhibitor of RIG-I/MAVS signalling.

title: IFN-alpha enhances TLR3-mediated antiviral cytokine expression in human endothelial and epithelial cells by up-regulating TLR3 expression.
claim_supported: Claim 1: IFN-alpha upregulates TLR3 expression in human A549 epithelial cells and HUVECs, i.e. TLR3 is interferon-inducible.

title: A diverse range of gene products are effectors of the type I interferon antiviral response.
claim_supported: Claim 1 (partial): overexpression screen of >380 human ISGs; the abstract names RIG-I (DDX58), MDA5 (IFIH1), C6orf150/MB21D1 (CGAS), IFI6, IFI44L, OASL and IFITM3 among ISG effectors.

title: Interferome v2.0: an updated database of annotated interferon-regulated genes.
claim_supported: Claim 1 (resource): Interferome v2.0 is a curated database of genes regulated by type I, II and III IFN in human and mouse cells and tissues, usable to check the ISG status of individual genes; the abstract does not list specific genes.

title: Shared and Distinct Functions of Type I and Type III Interferons.
claim_supported: Claim 2: type I and type III IFNs activate shared signalling pathways and transcriptional programs, with type III IFN acting as a front-line defence at epithelial barriers while limiting inflammation.

title: Local and systemic responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection in children and adults.
claim_supported: Healthy children's airway cells are in an interferon-activated state; because MHC-I processing genes are IFN-inducible (claim 4), age differences in M06 may partly track the IFN state (inference).

title: Mapping Bias Overestimates Reference Allele Frequencies at the HLA Genes in the 1000 Genomes Project Phase I Data.
claim_supported: Claim 5: reference mapping of short reads at HLA-A/-B/-C/-DRB1/-DQB1 gave 18.6% incorrect genotype calls with bias towards reference alleles (DNA-seq; the implication for HLA expression quantification in scRNA-seq is an extrapolation).

title: Towards a systems understanding of MHC class I and MHC class II antigen presentation.
claim_supported: Review of the molecular machinery of MHC class I antigen processing and presentation (proteasome, peptide transport and loading).

title: NLRC5: a key regulator of MHC class I-dependent immune responses.
claim_supported: Claim 4: review establishing NLRC5 as the MHC class I transactivator (CITA), the class I counterpart of CIITA.

title: A diverse range of gene products are effectors of the type I interferon antiviral response.
claim_supported: Claim 4: full text lists PSMB8 and PSMB9 among the ISGs tested in the type I IFN effector screen.

journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
title: NLR family member NLRC5 is a transcriptional regulator of MHC class I genes.
claim_supported: Claim 4: NLRC5 is IFN-gamma-inducible, binds and transactivates MHC-I promoters, is required for IFN-gamma-induced MHC-I upregulation, and also induces B2M, TAP and LMP (PSMB) genes.

title: Increased expression of HLA-DR and CD86 in nasal epithelial cells in allergic rhinitics: antigen presentation to T cells and up-regulation by diesel exhaust particles.
claim_supported: Nasal epithelial cells constitutively express HLA-DR, IFN-gamma upregulates it, and cultured nasal epithelial cells can drive antigen-specific autologous T-cell proliferation.

title: Epithelial MHC Class II Expression and Its Role in Antigen Presentation in the Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Tracts.
claim_supported: MHC class II is highly expressed on lung and intestinal epithelial cells, which may act as non-professional antigen-presenting cells.

title: HLA-DR and ICAM-1 expression and modulation in epithelial cells from nasal polyps.
claim_supported: Human nasal polyp epithelium stains for HLA-DR in situ, and IFN-gamma increases HLA-DR on cultured nasal epithelial cells.

title: Mapping Bias Overestimates Reference Allele Frequencies at the HLA Genes in the 1000 Genomes Project Phase I Data.
claim_supported: Claim 5: reference mapping bias at HLA-DRB1 and HLA-DQB1 (DNA-seq), so per-gene HLA class II counts from reference-aligned scRNA-seq may be biased between donors with different alleles.

title: The bare lymphocyte syndrome and the regulation of MHC expression.
claim_supported: MHC-II expression requires RFX (RFXANK, RFX5, RFXAP) and the master coactivator CIITA, whose defects cause bare lymphocyte syndrome.

title: Towards a systems understanding of MHC class I and MHC class II antigen presentation.
claim_supported: Review of the molecular machinery of MHC class II antigen presentation.

title: The lysosomal cysteine proteases in MHC class II antigen presentation.
claim_supported: Cathepsin S (CTSS) and cathepsin L degrade invariant chain (CD74) and process antigen in the MHC-II pathway; the abstract does not discuss legumain (LGMN).

title: Regulation of MHC class II expression by interferon-gamma mediated by the transactivator gene CIITA.
claim_supported: CIITA is induced by IFN-gamma, is required for MHC-II induction and is sufficient to activate MHC class II genes, i.e. it regulates both inducible and constitutive MHC-II.

title: Age-dependent dysregulation of innate immunity.
claim_supported: Innate immune cell functions such as cell migration and PRR signalling are impaired in aged individuals (review, not DC- or airway-specific).

title: Increased expression of HLA-DR and CD86 in nasal epithelial cells in allergic rhinitics: antigen presentation to T cells and up-regulation by diesel exhaust particles.
claim_supported: Human nasal epithelial cells constitutively express HLA-DR and CD86 but not CD80, and CD86 is upregulated by IL-1beta/TNF-alpha, so M08 scores in epithelium do not mean DC maturation.

title: A conserved dendritic-cell regulatory program limits antitumour immunity.
claim_supported: Claim 6: scRNA-seq in human and mouse lung cancer defined mregDCs co-expressing maturation genes (CD40, CCR7, IL12B) and immunoregulatory genes (CD274, PDCD1LG2, CD200), acquired by DC1 and DC2 after antigen uptake.

title: Immune functions and immunopathology of the mucosa of the upper respiratory pathways.
claim_supported: Claim 9: in upper airway mucosa memory B cells differentiate locally into Ig-producing plasma cells whose product is mainly J-chain-containing polymeric IgA, transported by pIgR/secretory component.

title: The generation of antibody-secreting plasma cells.
claim_supported: Review: plasmablast and plasma-cell differentiation from B cells is governed by a central gene-regulatory network (the abstract does not name individual genes).

title: BCMA is essential for the survival of long-lived bone marrow plasma cells.
claim_supported: BCMA (TNFRSF17) is expressed more highly in plasma cells than in resting B cells and is required for survival of long-lived bone-marrow plasma cells (mouse).

title: XBP1, downstream of Blimp-1, expands the secretory apparatus and other organelles, and increases protein synthesis in plasma cell differentiation.
claim_supported: Blimp-1 (PRDM1) is required to induce most plasma-cell genes including XBP1, and XBP1 induces secretory-pathway genes and expands the ER (mouse).

title: Blimp-1 is required for the formation of immunoglobulin secreting plasma cells and pre-plasma memory B cells.
claim_supported: B-cell-specific loss of Blimp-1 (PRDM1) abolishes Ig-secreting plasma cells and XBP-1 induction, and XBP-1 cannot rescue plasmacytic differentiation without Blimp-1 (mouse).

title: Immune functions and immunopathology of the mucosa of the upper respiratory pathways.
claim_supported: Claim 9: locally produced Ig in upper-airway mucosa consists mainly of polymeric IgA, while IgG reaches secretions largely by passive diffusion.

title: IgA subclass switch recombination in human mucosal and systemic immune compartments.
claim_supported: Human IgA1 and IgA2 switch recombination was profiled in nasal mucosa and other compartments; local IgA1/IgA2 proportions parallel IgA1+/IgA2+ plasma-cell distributions, supporting summing IGHA1 and IGHA2.

title: Role of J chain in secretory immunoglobulin formation.
claim_supported: Claim 9: J chain made by mucosal and glandular plasma cells is needed to form polymeric IgA/IgM with high affinity for pIgR, so JCHAIN plus pIgR are key to secretory IgA.

title: Survey of senescent cell markers with age in human tissues.
claim_supported: There is no universal senescence marker; p16 and p21 positive cells rose with age in several human organs but not in lung, so the age trend is tissue-specific.

title: Cellular Senescence: Defining a Path Forward.
claim_supported: Claim 10: International Cell Senescence Association consensus that accurate in vivo detection of senescent cells needs several markers combined (it proposes a multi-marker algorithm), so no single marker is sufficient.

title: Unmasking Transcriptional Heterogeneity in Senescent Cells.
claim_supported: Senescence markers (CDKN2A, CDKN1A, SASP, LMNB1 loss) are non-exclusive and the senescent transcriptome varies by inducer, cell type and time since induction.

title: A new gene set identifies senescent cells and predicts senescence-associated pathways across tissues.
claim_supported: Claim 10: full text states CDKN2A and CDKN1A were intentionally left out of the 125-gene SenMayo set (used to validate it), and CDKN2A mRNA is low and may not be reliably detected in scRNA-seq; IGFBP7 is a SenMayo SASP gene; SERPINE1 and GDF15 membership could not be confirmed (Supplementary Data 1 not accessible).

title: Cellular Senescence: Defining a Path Forward.
claim_supported: Claim 10: consensus definition of cellular senescence and recommended biomarkers (the abstract does not list individual genes).

title: A proteomic atlas of senescence-associated secretomes for aging biomarker development.
claim_supported: The SASP Atlas found GDF15 and SERPINs among proteins secreted by senescent cells that also correlate with age in human plasma (the abstract says 'SERPINs', not SERPINE1 by name).

title: Oncogenic BRAF induces senescence and apoptosis through pathways mediated by the secreted protein IGFBP7.
claim_supported: Secreted IGFBP7 is needed for BRAF-V600E oncogene-induced senescence in human fibroblasts and melanocytes.

title: Inflammaging: a new immune-metabolic viewpoint for age-related diseases.
claim_supported: Claim 11: inflammaging is the chronic, sterile, low-grade inflammation that develops with ageing and contributes to age-related disease.

title: Impaired local intrinsic immunity to SARS-CoV-2 infection in severe COVID-19.
claim_supported: Nasopharyngeal epithelial states change strongly with acute viral infection, so current infection status is a confounder for inflammatory and IFN module scores.

title: Chronic inflammation in the etiology of disease across the life span.
claim_supported: Systemic chronic inflammation is promoted by infections, inactivity, diet, toxicants and stress and underlies many diseases, so inflammatory cytokine expression is not specific to ageing.

title: Senescence-associated secretory phenotypes reveal cell-nonautonomous functions of oncogenic RAS and the p53 tumor suppressor.
claim_supported: Claim 11: defined the SASP: senescent fibroblasts and epithelial cells induced by genotoxic stress secrete many inflammatory factors, with IL-6 and IL-8 (CXCL8) as key paracrine mediators.

title: A new gene set identifies senescent cells and predicts senescence-associated pathways across tissues.
claim_supported: Full text: IL1A, CXCL8 and CCL2 are highly connected nodes of the SenMayo gene network, and CDKN1A, CCL2 and IL6 rose with age in two human bone cohorts.

title: Prolonged activation of nasal immune cell populations and development of tissue-resident SARS-CoV-2-specific CD8+ T cell responses following COVID-19.
claim_supported: Human nasal mucosa holds CD38+CD8+ TRM and SARS-CoV-2-specific CD8+ T cells that persisted at least 2 months after viral clearance.

title: Single-cell sequencing reveals dissociation-induced gene expression in tissue subpopulations.
claim_supported: Tissue dissociation induces gene-expression artefacts in scRNA-seq (from title only; no PubMed abstract, so whether CD69 or DUSP6 are affected was not verified here).

title: Human Tissue-Resident Memory T Cells Are Defined by Core Transcriptional and Functional Signatures in Lymphoid and Mucosal Sites.
claim_supported: Full text: CD101 is not in the 31-gene core; it was a lung-specific transcript, raised on CD8+CD69+ cells by flow but minimally on CD4+ TRM, and CD103 (ITGAE) is mainly CD8 TRM, so these genes bias the score to CD8 TRM.

title: Human Tissue-Resident Memory T Cells Are Defined by Core Transcriptional and Functional Signatures in Lymphoid and Mucosal Sites.
claim_supported: Full text: the 31-gene core TRM signature (CD69+ vs CD69- memory T cells, lung and spleen, CD4 and CD8) includes upregulated ITGAE, ITGA1, CXCR6, PDCD1, DUSP6, CRTAM, IL2 and IL10 and downregulated S1PR1, KLF2, KLF3, SELL, CX3CR1, RAP1GAP1 and RGS1; CD69 defines the subset.

title: Resident memory CD8+ T cells in the upper respiratory tract prevent pulmonary influenza virus infection.
claim_supported: Nasal-epithelium CD8+ TRM persist long term and block influenza spread from the upper to the lower respiratory tract (mouse).
